lead: hired for the opening weeks — the setting up, the part before anyone knows where anything lives — and by the ninth day you can name which two of them the place is running on.
sun: the reading needs a position rather than a tenure, which is what catches people out about you. from half inside a crew the seams are what show — which of the managers the room looks at, which part of the work would still happen if nobody were watching, which part is somebody's fondness with a budget line. none of that waits for a second year, and you were never going to have one.
moon: and it goes out the same day. what The Gate lands in you announces itself immediately and at one volume, whether it is the thing that will sink the branch or a bad fortnight in one man's marriage, and you are right often enough that the misses are the memorable part. a call made in the second week has nothing standing behind it except that you made it.
pull: the crew you have known for nine days sorts cleanly into the two it runs on and the rest, and you will be at another opening before anybody there finds out you were right.
tension: an outfit puts a new person on probation for a season so that nobody's reading of it counts until they have earned the right to one. yours is finished before the paperwork is. the accurate thing therefore arrives from someone with no stake in living with it, and the word that comes back is blunt, and underneath the word sits the real objection — you will be gone before the consequences are.
cost: a place about to come apart for a reason nobody inside could name gets told the reason in a month, by somebody brought in to hang doors, and that is why the calls keep coming. what you said in the second week is still deciding who gets the good jobs at a firm whose name you would now have to look up.

lead: you worked out at seventeen which of them the house was standing on, and which of its stories was doing the work, and you have never said either thing to anybody in it.
sun: a family is the one body you were placed inside rather than joined, and you were at that table before you could weigh anything, which ought to make the seeing impossible. it did not. from the end of it the structure is plain — which marriage is carrying the other two, which of them everybody is quietly covering for, which of the stories about your grandfather is the one holding the rest up. nobody asked.
moon: nothing here has ever come out sideways. The Bearer holds to term and releases on a decision — no bad night emptied you, no drink loosened it, no argument dragged it into the room. thirty years of that, and the sorting has stopped being a live thing you are carrying. it sits in you now the way stored goods sit, dated, in a condition nobody has checked.
pull: a verdict on your own family, complete since your teens, kept whole, and nobody it concerns has ever heard a word of it — including the ones it would have cleared.
tension: even-handed comes back at you, and fair, and the one who does not take sides, said with relief by people who have watched the rest of them take sides for decades. you are not neutral. you decided early and the decision has simply never had an outlet, so what reads as generosity is a full account withheld. two of them came to you separately for a ruling and both left believing they had one.
cost: every part of that family still opens the door to you, which is what comes of sitting through a version of your own childhood you know is wrong and correcting no sentence of it, at every gathering, for thirty years. what you are holding has aged badly. the arrangement it describes came apart twenty years ago, and two of the people weighed in it are dead.

lead: the amount gets said as one amount. it comes out of six wallets, it has never once been said as six, and nobody else paying into it has ever done the arithmetic.
sun: The Flock puts the sorting onto the ledger rather than onto the people, which is how it has stayed sayable this long. you can name which of the standing costs is holding the arrangement up and which is a habit left over from a decade when there was more, and you are naming it about money that three other adults are also paying in. nobody appointed you to it. being on the list was enough.
moon: from any distance the pot is one object with one name, and the one name is the mechanism: nobody has to feel carried, because nothing in it belongs to anyone in particular. up close it resolves: two of the names are the thing, one arrives late and counts the same. a short year does that resolving out loud, in front of everybody, whether or not you say a word.
pull: one figure, spoken as one figure for a decade, and the season it falls short it comes apart into the people who were paying and the people who were present.
tension: the arithmetic costs more than the shortfall does. a single figure is what lets people who love each other unevenly sit in the same room without a reckoning, and said as several figures it does not go back — every gathering afterwards has amounts in it. it was never about the money is what returns to you, from the two it was most about, and neither of them is lying.
cost: the thin year did not finish the arrangement, because what got cut was ornamental and nobody had to be told which parts those were. your own share disappears into the single figure alongside everybody's, and the figure stays single only while the one person who can see through it says nothing about what is inside.

lead: nobody at that table has ever worried about you. you have been one place behind the heaviest appetite in the room since you were twenty-two, and one place behind reads as moderation from every angle.
sun: bodies are what the sorting lands on here, and it lands early. you can say which two of that crew it is taking — from the colour of one, from what the other stopped doing on sundays — while the crew is still calling it a good stretch and getting the next round in. you are on the list you made. putting yourself on it has never been the same as coming off it.
moon: The Follower took second position deliberately and has never conceded it. staying one place behind whoever is at the top of a room is a way of being fully inside it and never the one it is about, and the reckoning of you is always somebody else's, minus one. what a body does with a quantity takes no interest in whose pace set it. it keeps what it was handed.
pull: you can say which two at that table it will take. you have matched one of them evening for evening for eleven years, and your name is on nobody's list of the worried-about.
tension: you told one of them once, plainly and correctly, and he stopped coming, and the crew closed over the space inside a month and now says he went strange. that is the entire record of you acting on any of this. what gets said about you is sensible, and the one to ask for a lift home, and it gets said by people who have only ever seen you in a room where everyone is at the same rate.
cost: two of them have been discussed at length in that room, with real worry, and you have not come up once — a decade inside a shared habit and never the one anybody counts. the body counted. the pace belonged to whoever was loudest in whichever room, the accumulation belongs entirely to you, and none of it was ever put down anywhere else.
